indicators.note: the letters read the same when turned round and read from the far end, just as they do forwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A traveller finds rooms and does the same again on the way home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'likewise on return' says the entry is unchanged when read backwards: a palindrome, so the definition is the only other clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To be put up somewhere is to be given a bed for the night, so the phrase means to lodge.

definitions.meaning: Sir Bernard ... was a leading Punch cartoonist; the 's stands for is
in The Twelve Days of Christmas the first day's gift is a bird in a pear tree

explanation.surface: An artist's first festive present.
explanation.walkthrough: Bernard Partridge drew cartoons for Punch, the British humorous magazine, for over fifty years.
explanation.definitionFit: A Punch cartoonist shared his surname with the game bird given on the first day of the carol.

indicators.note: about means the upturned word surrounds the order abbreviation

parts.note: read as up-set: the word set written upwards in a down entry
OM is the Order of Merit

explanation.surface: A tipped-over display is put back in order for the library.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' is split as 'up set': in a down entry SET reads upwards as TES, which goes round OM.
explanation.definitionFit: Large heavy volumes are weighty books.

parts.note: pop's means father's, pa's
sable is a costly dark fur

explanation.surface: Dad's fur coat is all right, just about.
explanation.definitionFit: Something adequate is tolerable, acceptable rather than good.

clue.text: Shells corps retiring quickly to the south

indicators.note: troops retiring fall back, so the abbreviation for the corps is written backwards

parts.note: RAC is the Royal Armoured Corps
apace is an old word for quickly

explanation.surface: Artillery shells fall as an army corps retreats hurriedly southward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shells' and 'corps' paint a battlefield, but shells here are hard animal casings. 'retiring' turns RAC into CAR; APACE and S follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A tortoise or crab carries a hard upper casing, the protective shell on its back.

definitions.meaning: to trim with scissors or shears
a fast pace, as in going at a good rate

explanation.surface: Slashed at a great rate.
explanation.definitionFit: To trim is to snip short; a fast rate of movement is also a brisk pace.

indicators.note: chopping breaks up the letters of the phrase sound trees and reassembles them

explanation.surface: A lumberjack wears himself out felling healthy trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopping' rearranges SOUND TREES.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant gone to seed has stopped producing and is spent, so the phrase means to decline.

definitions.meaning: taken as parts that are good for looking with, the openings in the eyes
a school form is a class, filled by its children

explanation.surface: Handsome people completing paperwork.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools a 'form' is a class, so its members fill it. The eyes' dark centres are what we look through.
explanation.definitionFit: Schoolchildren make up a class, and the dark apertures of the eyes let in light for sight.

clue.text: Light repast sly fellow eats it all up

indicators.note: eats means the fellow's word takes the other letters inside itself

parts.note: coon is an old American word for a sly, knowing fellow, from raccoon

indicators.note: up means the words it all are read upwards, backwards in a down entry

explanation.surface: A cunning man devours the entire light meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses IT ALL to LLATI, which 'eats' places inside COON. The old slang word is now offensive.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold collation is a light meal of cold foods.

clue.text: We put in some tennis, of course

indicators.note: put in means the pronoun is placed inside the tennis word

parts.note: a set is a portion of a tennis match
taken as written

explanation.surface: We fit in a little tennis, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' reads as 'naturally', but the definition is 'course', a stage of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dessert is the closing dish of a meal, a course after the main.

parts.note: remiss means careless in one's duty

indicators.note: including means the batting word holds the duck letter within it

parts.note: a cricketer who is batting is said to be in
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so O

explanation.surface: A careless cricketer, out for nought, is let off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' puts O inside IN, giving ION after REMISS. A duck is a cricket score of zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Remission is the cancelling of a penalty or debt, a form of forgiveness.

parts.note: felt reads as the fabric, but a doctor feels a sick patient's wrist to count the heartbeat

explanation.surface: Someone shows sympathy for a sick person.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor checks a sick patient's heartbeat by touching the wrist, the throb that is felt.

parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation: Hamlet's soliloquy in Act 2 calls himself a dull and muddy-mettled something, a word for a scoundrel

explanation.surface: A line from Hamlet with its last word left out for the solver to supply.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan prints 'muddy-mettled', mangled to 'settled-' in the OCR. In Act 2, Hamlet says 'Yet I, a dull and muddy-mettled rascal, peak like John-a-dreams'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet's self-reproach uses the word for a mischievous scoundrel to complete the line.

clue.text: Resolute type returns to fish at the Pole

indicators.note: returns means the whole string after it comes back, read from right to left

parts.note: to trawl is to fish with a net dragged behind a boat
S stands for the South Pole

explanation.surface: A determined explorer goes back to fishing at the South Pole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' reverses all of TRAWL AT S together.
explanation.definitionFit: A staunch, dependable supporter is a firm and loyal person.

indicators.note: order means the letters of bitter aloe are arranged anew

explanation.surface: A demand to remove a bitter plant medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' rearranges BITTER ALOE.
explanation.definitionFit: To wipe out completely is to remove every trace.

clue.text: May be a plucked 'un, far from highly-strung

definitions.text: May be a plucked 'un, far from highly-strung

parts.words: May be a plucked 'un, far from highly-strung
parts.note: plucked 'un suggests a brave person, highly-strung a nervous one; really it is a big string instrument that is plucked and pitched very low

explanation.surface: A gutsy character who is anything but nervy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plucky' and 'highly-strung' describe temperament; read musically, the strings are plucked and tuned to the lowest notes of the orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest and lowest of the orchestra's bowed strings is often plucked in jazz.

parts.note: stress means emphasise; the rest reads as a track that runs beneath the ground

explanation.surface: Strain on an underground train system.
explanation.walkthrough: A line below the ground is literally 'under line'; to emphasise text is to draw a line under it.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawing a rule beneath words emphasises them, so it means to stress.

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Salted meat is kept for later.
explanation.definitionFit: Canned food is kept in metal containers, so the plural noun names preserved goods' containers.

indicators.note: something needing repair is broken, so the letters of places etc are rearranged

explanation.surface: Show venues and so on are in a poor state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing repair' rearranges PLACES ETC.
explanation.definitionFit: A striking public display or performance is a show.

definitions.meaning: undiluted, as a drink served without water
a poker hand of five cards in a run

explanation.surface: A tidy, convenient series.
explanation.walkthrough: 'handy' means relating to a hand of cards: in poker this is five cards in numerical order.
explanation.definitionFit: Whisky served undiluted is taken this way; in poker a run of five consecutive cards forms this hand.

parts.note: Hamlet says there is a divinity that shapes our ... a line closing on the word for extremities or final outcomes

explanation.surface: Fingers and toes formed by the hand of God.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet, Act 5: 'There's a divinity that shapes our ends, rough-hew them how we will.'
explanation.definitionFit: Tips and terminations are the far points of anything, the extremities.

clue.text: Casual amateur, sees poet about new title

indicators.note: about means the poet's name goes round the other letters

parts.note: Dante Alighieri was the Italian poet of the Divine Comedy

indicators.note: new means the letters of the word title are made over into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A dabbler notices a famous poet's book getting a new name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns TITLE into ILETT, and 'about' puts DANTE round it after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A dabbler takes up an art for pleasure without serious skill or commitment.

clue.text: A sort of post box, sort of

definitions.text: A sort of post box, sort of

parts.words: A sort of post box, sort of
parts.note: a type of upright post, and the red British mailbox named after such a column

explanation.surface: Some kind of mailbox, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: The British roadside red post box is called a pillar box; the word alone is also a kind of post or column.
explanation.definitionFit: A column is a kind of upright post, and it names the British red roadside mailbox.

definitions.meaning: the armed forces: army, navy and air force together
on a tennis court, each player's shots that start a point

explanation.surface: Military people take legal action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court actions' looks legal; it means tennis serves.
explanation.definitionFit: The armed services are the military; in tennis, serves are the strokes that begin each rally.

clue.text: Blows for the southern race circuits

parts.note: laps are circuits of a racetrack

explanation.surface: A southern race meeting is a setback.
explanation.definitionFit: Smacks with the open hand are blows.

clue.text: Make mistake in label — put back in attic

indicators.note: put back means the whole construction is written in reverse order
in means the mistake word sits inside the label word

parts.note: a tag is a label tied on
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: A misprinted tag is returned to the loft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts ERR inside TAG to make TERRAG; 'put back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A small room just under the roof, often a poor artist's lodging, is a loft.

indicators.note: centre of picks the middle letters of the word strife

parts.note: the sky is the heavens

explanation.surface: In the thick of conflict, someone exclaims at the peril.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre of' takes the middle pair RI from STRIFE; 'Heavens!' looks like an exclamation but gives SKY.
explanation.definitionFit: Hazardous means full of danger, a chance of harm.

definitions.meaning: a child calls dibs on something by saying this word, as in I claim first go

explanation.surface: A pupil lays claim to the suitcases.
explanation.walkthrough: British schoolchildren say 'bags I' to claim something first.
explanation.definitionFit: Shouting it claims first right to something, and cases carried on a journey are baggage.

clue.text: Prisoner'" pined '" for release by Prospero

definitions.text: Prisoner'" pined '" for release by Prospero

parts.words: Prisoner'" pined '" for release by Prospero
parts.note: pined seems to mean yearned, but in The Tempest the spirit was imprisoned in a cloven pine tree until Prospero freed it

explanation.surface: A prisoner longs for Prospero to set him free.
explanation.walkthrough: In The Tempest the witch Sycorax shut the spirit in a pine tree; Prospero released it, so 'pined' means locked in pine.
explanation.definitionFit: The airy spirit serving Prospero in The Tempest had been confined in a pine before he freed it.

clue.text: Bill included a single wrong number?

indicators.note: included means the bill's letters hold the others between them

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill

indicators.note: wrong means the letters of a single are put into the wrong order

explanation.surface: An invoice listing one incorrect telephone number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' reads as a figure, but here it is something that numbs. 'wrong' shuffles A SINGLE into NALGESI, which 'included' puts inside AC.
explanation.definitionFit: A painkiller deadens feeling, so it is something that numbs.

clue.text: Characteristic of precipice in Isle of Sheppey

definitions.meaning: a cliff's defining quality is its steep vertical drop
a port town on the Isle of Sheppey in Kent, England

explanation.surface: A cliff typical of the Kent island.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Sheppey is an island off the north Kent coast; its main port shares its name with the quality of steepness.
explanation.definitionFit: A precipice is notable for its steepness; the Kent port on Sheppey bears the same name.

indicators.note: say means the word is to be pronounced, giving a herb spelt differently

parts.note: a season is a time of year

explanation.surface: A herb that is in season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'season' tempts as cooking flavour; it is a period, and 'say' gives the herb that sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A low aromatic plant of the mint family is used in cooking as a herb.
